Q: How to save file from $request in Laravel? A:

You can use Laravel storage: https://laravel.com/docs/8.x/filesystem#the-public-disk

You just need 3 basic steps:

  1. create symbolic link from command: php artisan storage:link
  2. config your file system in the config directory: public_path('storage') => storage_path('app/public')
  3. save file: Storage::disk('public')->put('file_name', 'file');

Q: Heroku-Connect with Postgres and Salesforce : The new rows are not synchronized A:

The error is coming from a Salesforce Process Builder flow ("Opportunity - Owner Assignment") that fires on insert, not from Heroku Connect itself. Even though you're setting ownerid in your INSERT, Heroku Connect strips certain fields during the write back to Salesforce because it manages them through its own mapping layer. The ownerid and createdbyid fields are typically treated as read only by Heroku Connect on inserts, meaning Salesforce receives the record without an owner, which then causes the Process Builder flow to fail with INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY.

To fix this you have a couple options. First, check your Heroku Connect mapping for the Opportunity object and confirm that ownerid is included in the mapped columns and that the "Write to Salesforce" direction is enabled for that specific field. If its greyed out or not writable, Heroku Connect wont send it. Second, look at the Process Builder flow in Salesforce Setup under Process Automation and either add a null check for OwnerId before the assignment step, or set a default owner in the flow logic so it doesnt fail on records coming from Heroku.

-- Also make sure you have an External ID field mapped, which is required
-- for Heroku Connect to write new records back to Salesforce
INSERT INTO salesforce.opportunity (
  name, closedate, stagename, ownerid, external_id__c
)
VALUES (
  'zzzz', '2021-12-31', 'New', '0051t000002VZvKAAW', 'HC-OPP-001'
);

As the other answer mentioned, you need a Unique External ID field on the Opportunity object in Salesforce thats mapped in Heroku Connect with "Write database updates to Salesforce" enabled. Without that, Heroku Connect cant match new Postgres rows to Salesforce records for the upsert operation (https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/heroku-connect-database-tables).

That said, this kind of issue is pretty typical with Heroku Connect once you go beyond simple read syncs. The field mapping restrictions, External ID requirements, and conflicts with Salesforce automation (flows, Process Builder, triggers) make bidirectional sync painful to debug. Full disclosure, I'm the CEO of Stacksync and we've replaced Heroku Connect for a number of teams hitting exactly these problems. It handles the Salesforce field permissions and automation conflicts natively so you dont have to work around them, and it works with any Postgres host so you're not locked into Heroku's ecosystem

Q: Data structures A:

Which sense are you searching for. In my head there are two questions that students tend to ask, and I am probably missing a lot:

  1. The one you are asking: why does the code work?
  2. What will I need this for? What is the use case for, say, a stack?

Some focus on one, others on the other, some indispensably need answers to both.

For why your code works, drawing on paper as suggested, has helped myself a long way. You will also find illustrative animations on the net.

For what you need them for, the practice may be harder, start out from real world cases and try to figure out which data structure would fit the data that you need to keep and the search patterns along which you need to retrieve them.

Q: Right align texts in Canvas using Jetpack Compose A:

You measure the text based on the string characters only. But when you actually display the text you modify its size, so the calculation using the TextMeasurer is off.

Simply also include the style in the calculation, and everything works out:

val yAxisLabelMaxWidth = textMeasurer.measure(text = "${max.toInt()}", style = style).size.width.toFloat()
val yAxisLabelMinWidth = textMeasurer.measure(text = "${min.toInt()}", style = style).size.width.toFloat()

For that you should extract the style into a dedicated variable to prevent writing the same piece of code four times:

val style = TextStyle(
    fontSize = 10.sp,
    background = Color.Green,
)

You should probably do the same for the texts.

Q: mysqldump & gzip commands to properly create a compressed file of a MySQL database using crontab A:

Personally, I have create a file.sh (right 755) in the root directory, file who do this job, on order of the crontab.

Crontab code:

10 2 * * * root /root/backupautomatique.sh

File.sh code:

rm -f /home/mordb-148-251-89-66.sql.gz #(To erase the old one)

mysqldump mor | gzip > /home/mordb-148-251-89-66.sql.gz (what you have done)

scp -P2222 /home/mordb-148-251-89-66.sql.gz root@otherip:/home/mordbexternes/mordb-148-251-89-66.sql.gz

(to send a copy somewhere else if the sending server crashes, because too old, like me ;-))
